records.name_note: The stored name is a genus, not a binomial. The cited care values come from sources covering Schlumbergera × buckleyi, the true Christmas cactus. A large share of plants sold as 'Christmas cactus' are actually S. truncata (Thanksgiving or crab cactus), which Missouri Botanical Garden treats separately; S. truncata has pointed teeth on the stem segments where S. × buckleyi has rounded scallops. If the plant is S. truncata these values should be re-verified against a S. truncata source.
records.cool_rest_note: Bud set requires a deliberate cool, long-night trigger beginning in mid-September: night temperatures of 55 to 65 F together with at least 13 hours of completely uninterrupted darkness every night, plus bright light during the day. Watering is reduced at the same time. Even brief light at night (a lamp, a hallway light) can prevent flowering. The 55-65 F figures recorded in night_f_min/night_f_max are this bud-set requirement, not a year-round night range.
records.water_dry_down_target: Evenly moist spring through summer, neither soggy nor bone dry; reduce watering from mid-September through the bud-set period.

This is an epiphyte in an airy mix, so it dries faster than its 'keep moist' regime suggests; the longer figure applies to the mid-September onward rest period when the source calls for reduced watering.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State Extension states the plant is non-toxic and can be safely kept in homes with pets or children. This is an explicit non-toxicity statement, not an inference from silence.
